title: Dedicated capacity onboarding playbook: customer profiles & conditional fallback policies
creator: Lena Morales
description: Create a pragmatic, repeatable playbook for triaging enterprise dedicated capacity requests. The playbook should produce a deterministic recommended intake outcome: recommended SLA band (latency & uptime), reserved throughput (tokens/sec / concurrent streams), GPU class (A100/H100/RTX/latent-quantized variants), and conditional autoscale & fallback policies. Deliverables: 1) intake questionnaire template, 2) scoring rubric that maps answers to capacity profiles, 3) decision matrix for fallbacks (model variant, region, degraded SLOs), 4) sample onboarding runbook and handoff checklist for Solutions/Support.
acceptance_criteria: Intake questionnaire (Confluence link) populated and validated with 3 pilot customers
Scoring rubric documented and reproducible (spreadsheet + formula) producing consistent profile outputs
Decision matrix maps every high-priority risk (bursting, preemption, KV-cache sensitivity, PII/data residency) to a recommended conditional fallback
Onboarding runbook includes handoff steps for billing, security review, and initial 72-hour watch with monitoring queries
Stakeholder sign-off from sales-eng, infra-ops, and security on playbook gating criteria
steps: Draft intake questionnaire focusing on workload signals: qps/75th/95th latency SLO, peak concurrency, token distribution, streaming vs batch, stateful KV cache needs, model determinism/temperature requirements, PII/residency constraints

Design scoring rubric: weight token/sec and concurrency more heavily for throughput-first customers; weight latency SLA for user-facing chat apps; penalize non-resumable KV-heavy workloads when recommending preemptible GPUs
Prototype mapping: produce 6 capacity profiles (dev, low, standard, high-throughput, latency-priority, regulated) and tie to GPU classes and reservation sizes

Define autoscale & fallback policies per profile: e.g., latency-priority -> reserved pool + burst credit; standard -> shared pool with canary fallback to smaller model variant; regulated -> private/VPC only, no multi-tenant bursting
Run 3 pilot intakes with existing mid-market customers, record observed vs predicted SLOs and adjust weights
Create handoff checklist for Solutions Eng -> Infra for provisioning, include billing tags and monitoring dashboards
Publish final playbook to Confluence and present to GTM + infra for adoption
comments: 2025-02-18 Lena Morales: Initial intake ticket created after QBR with Enterprise Sales. Primary asks: predictable latency SLAs and clear GPU recommendations. Noted recurring customer pattern: bursty query traffic with KV-heavy reranking.
2025-02-20 Diego Rios: Drafted questionnaire v0.1 and posted to Confluence. Requested feedback from Solutions Eng and Runtime team. Linked PR for rubric template.

2025-02-24 Priya Shah (Solutions Eng): Reviewed questionnaire. Feedback: add explicit question about determinism (temperature/seed) and fallback acceptance for quantized models. Also requested example of expected token distribution (p50/p95).

2025-02-26 Marcus Lee (Runtime): Confirmed GPU class mapping is over-simplified. Proposed adding constraint for KV-cache sensitive models that prefer H100/64GB SRAM-like instances. Suggested a small experiment to measure latency delta at 2k vs 8k context lengths.

2025-03-01 Diego Rios: Completed pilot intake with Customer ACME Analytics. Scored as 'standard' profile but required hybrid: reserved baseline + burst credits. Observed prediction error: underestimated peak concurrency by 20%. Adjusted weighting: +15% weight to customer-provided peak concurrency sample.
2025-03-03 Security (Ana Gomez): Reviewed playbook. Flagged: any 'regulated' profile must include explicit KMS/HSM key ownership step and audit log ingestion; added to handoff checklist.

2025-03-04 Lena Morales: Updated acceptance criteria and scheduled review with Sales/Infra for 2025-03-07. Next actions: finalize rubric, run one controlled synthetic load test for KV-heavy model to validate GPU recommendation.
notes: Trade-offs: aggressive reservation reduces cold-start risk but increases cost; the rubric surfaces a 'cost-risk score' to help Sales negotiate commit levels.

Fallback design: prefer model-variant fallback (quantized / smaller architecture) when possible; region fallback only when data residency allows; last resort is degraded latency SLO with a customer-approved grace period.
Known unknowns: exact mapping between preemption probability and customer tolerance; need telemetry from Dedicated pools to tune burst credit sizing
